about: The kinds of mechanism found in the surveyed sets' functions. Each curated function in data/sets/<set>.json lists its kinds in `mechanisms`, each a kind's `kind`, optionally followed by a colon and a short detail ("driving-ring-gearbox: 4 speeds", "piston-engine: V8"). A kind is added when a function's mechanism fits none of these without stretching; the catalog in docs/mechanisms/ is generated from them by npm run mechanisms.

kinds.name: Rack and pinion steering
kinds.means: A pinion slides a toothed rack across, and the rack pushes the steering arms.

kinds.name: Linkage steering
kinds.means: An arm, crank or gear at the foot of the steering column pushes the tie rods or steering arms directly, with no rack.

kinds.name: Swivelling axle steering
kinds.means: The whole axle or wheel unit turns on an upright pivot.

kinds.name: Articulated steering
kinds.means: The machine bends at an upright hinge between its front and rear halves.

kinds.name: Multi-axle steering
kinds.means: More than one axle steers: the rear wheels steer too, or two front axles steer together.

kinds.name: Steering mode selector
kinds.means: A knob or lever sets how the rear wheels steer: against the front ones, not at all, or with them (four-wheel, front-only or crab steering).

kinds.name: Fork steering
kinds.means: Handlebars turn the whole fork with its wheel or ski, as on a motorbike.

kinds.name: Skid steering
kinds.means: The tracks or wheels on each side are driven separately, so the machine turns by driving them at different speeds.

kinds.name: Rudder
kinds.means: A rudder at the stern swings to steer a boat.

kinds.name: Swing arm
kinds.means: One arm carries the rear wheel, both rear wheels or the whole rear unit, pivoting ahead of it on a cross axle.

kinds.name: Trailing arms
kinds.means: Each wheel rides on an arm of its own, pivoting ahead of it.

kinds.name: Double wishbone suspension
kinds.means: Each wheel's hub rides between an upper and a lower arm.

kinds.name: Pushrod suspension
kinds.means: Wishbones with a pushrod to a rocker that works a shock absorber inboard.

kinds.name: Pendular axle
kinds.means: A rigid axle swings side to side on a central pivot or turntable.

kinds.name: Oscillating chassis
kinds.means: The chassis is split into front and rear halves that twist against each other about a lengthwise pivot, so all the wheels stay on rough ground.

kinds.name: Sprung live axle
kinds.means: A rigid axle hung on shock absorbers and links, free to tilt and rise.

kinds.name: Telescopic fork
kinds.means: The wheel slides up and down between two shock absorbers, as on a motorbike.

kinds.name: Telelever
kinds.means: A motorbike's front fork is held by an arm pivoting under the tank, with a shock absorber between the arm and the frame, so the wheel rises and falls.

kinds.name: Bogie
kinds.means: Two axles or wheels rock together on one pivot, sharing the load.

kinds.name: Track suspension
kinds.means: A track's idler or rollers ride on sprung arms.

kinds.name: Differential
kinds.means: Lets two shafts driven by one turn at different speeds, as the wheels on an axle do in a corner.

kinds.name: Differential lock
kinds.means: A driving ring locks a differential, so its two sides turn together.

kinds.name: Planetary hub
kinds.means: A planetary gear set in the wheel or sprocket hub slows its turn.

kinds.name: Portal axle
kinds.means: Gears in the hub drop the wheel below the axle's line, for ground clearance.

kinds.name: Chain drive
kinds.means: A chain runs round sprockets.

kinds.name: Belt drive
kinds.means: A rubber band or belt runs round pulleys.

kinds.name: Crawler tracks
kinds.means: Tracks run round sprockets and idlers.

kinds.name: Track tensioner
kinds.means: A screw or worm slides a track's idler to tighten or slacken the track.

kinds.name: Worm drive
kinds.means: A worm turns a gear, slowly, and holds it where it's left.

kinds.name: Slip clutch
kinds.means: A clutch gear or band slips when the part it drives can go no further, at the end of its travel or held.

kinds.name: Swinging idler clutch
kinds.means: An idler gear on a swinging arm is pulled into mesh when driven one way and kicked out of mesh the other way, so the drive only works in one direction.

kinds.name: Power take-off
kinds.means: The vehicle's drive turns an output for an implement: a tractor's power take-off shaft, a harrow, a combine's reel.

kinds.name: Sliding-gear gearbox
kinds.means: Speeds are chosen by sliding gears into and out of mesh.

kinds.name: Driving-ring gearbox
kinds.means: Speeds, ranges, or forward and reverse are chosen by sliding driving rings onto clutch gears, with a lever or in an H gate.

kinds.name: Sequential gearbox
kinds.means: A rotary catch, turned a step at a time, slides the driving rings through the gears in order.

kinds.name: Function selector
kinds.means: A driving ring, sliding gear or lever chooses which function one motor or knob drives, which way, or whether it drives it at all.

kinds.name: Rack and pinion
kinds.means: A pinion drives a toothed rack in a straight line, for anything but steering: forks, seats, booms, boards.

kinds.name: Linear actuator
kinds.means: A screw drives a piston out and in.

kinds.name: Pneumatic cylinder
kinds.means: Air let in by a valve pushes a cylinder out or in.

kinds.name: Crank and link
kinds.means: A crank or lever moves a part through links: a toggle, bellcrank, push rod or four-bar linkage.

kinds.name: Scissor linkage
kinds.means: Lazy tongs that stretch out and fold back.

kinds.name: Push-pull cable
kinds.means: A flexible cable sliding in a sleeve, as in the Flex System, carries a push or pull round corners to a distant part.

kinds.name: Winch
kinds.means: A drum winds a string or cable, over pulleys, to a hook, a grab or a boom.

kinds.name: Turntable
kinds.means: A part slews round on a turntable or an upright pivot, geared or by hand.

kinds.name: Three-point hitch
kinds.means: Lift arms raise and lower a tractor's implement on two lower links and a top link, keeping it upright.

kinds.name: Telescopic mast
kinds.means: A mast in stages: as one stage rises, a string or chain over a pulley at its top lifts the next stage or the carriage further.

kinds.name: Hook lift
kinds.means: An arm with a hook at its top swings back over the rear to set a container down behind the truck or pull it up onto the bed.

kinds.name: Rotary tool
kinds.means: The drive spins a working tool: a bucket wheel, drill, saw, auger, brush or mixer drum.

kinds.name: Conveyor
kinds.means: A belt or chain of treads runs round rollers to carry a load along.

kinds.name: Pop-up headlights
kinds.means: The headlights tip up out of the bodywork and fold back down, by hand or from a knob.

kinds.name: Piston engine
kinds.means: A crankshaft runs pistons up and down in their cylinders, a model engine.

kinds.name: Valve train
kinds.means: A camshaft lifts push rods and rockers to open the valves.

kinds.name: Driven rotor
kinds.means: The drive spins a propeller, rotor or fan: rolling the model, a knob, a motor or another rotor.

kinds.name: Rotor blade pitch
kinds.means: A collective or cyclic control twists the rotor blades or tilts the rotor head.

kinds.name: Control surfaces
kinds.means: A stick or pedals work the ailerons, elevators or rudder through rods and links.

kinds.name: Retractable landing gear
kinds.means: A crank, knob or motor swings the landing gear legs up into the airframe and down again.

kinds.name: Swing wings
kinds.means: The wings pivot near their roots to sweep back and forward together.

kinds.name: Electric motor
kinds.means: An electric motor drives the function.

kinds.name: Remote control
kinds.means: The motors are worked from a distance: infrared, a Bluetooth hub or an app.

kinds.name: Pneumatic pump
kinds.means: A pump, worked by hand or by a motor, fills the pneumatic system with air.

kinds.name: Pull-back motor
kinds.means: A spring motor wound by pulling the model back drives it forward when let go.

kinds.name: Stored-energy launcher
kinds.means: A bungee, rubber band or spring, once released, launches or flicks something.

kinds.name: Ratchet
kinds.means: A pawl on a gear lets it turn one way only until it's lifted.

kinds.name: Friction brake
kinds.means: A friction pin or a stiffly turning gear holds a part where it's left.

kinds.name: Catch
kinds.means: A latch, lock or detent holds a part in place until it's released.

kinds.name: Spring
kinds.means: A spring or rubber band holds a part up, pulls it back, or springs it back once pushed.

kinds.name: Free wheels
kinds.means: Wheels, rollers, a propeller or another part roll or spin freely, driven by nothing.

kinds.name: Hinge
kinds.means: A part swings on a hinge or pivot, by hand or turned straight at its pivot: a door, a bonnet, a folding leg, a hitch.

kinds.name: Slide
kinds.means: A part slides by hand, or under its own weight.

kinds.name: Posable joint
kinds.means: Ball joints, click hinges or friction joints that hold a pose.

kinds.name: Hangs free
kinds.means: A part swings free under gravity: a hook, claw or bucket hangs straight, a tailgate falls open.

kinds.name: Rigid
kinds.means: A structure that holds its shape: nothing in it moves.

kinds.name: For show
kinds.means: A control or part that looks as if it works something but isn't linked to anything.

kinds.name: Driven detail
kinds.means: Another function also turns a decorative part, such as an exhaust stack, beacon or radar, just to show it moving.

kinds.name: Accessory
kinds.means: A loose item that comes with the model.

kinds.name: Removable part
kinds.means: A part of the model lifts off or unclips by hand, to show or reach what's underneath.

kinds.name: Lights and electrics
kinds.means: Lights, fibre optics or switches that only work electrically.
